capability.evidence: Dropping 8 MLP layers: Llama-2-13B avg 68.2 -> 61.9, while dropping 8 attention layers gives 68.1 (Table 1); Mistral-7B MLP-8 70.3 -> 53.4 (Table 1); Llama-2-70B MLP-32 73.9 -> 55.7 (Table 3)
capability.citation: He, Sun, Shen, Li (2024), What Matters in Transformers? Not All Attention is Needed, arXiv:2406.15786 (preprint)
capability.note: Largest measured quality loss of any sublayer. Llama-2/Mistral, not Pythia. Mechanism: Geva et al. (2021), EMNLP, FFN as key-value memories (no ablation number).

capability.evidence: Dropping attention layers (attention layer + its LayerNorm): Llama-2-13B Attn-20 68.2 -> 64.9; Llama-2-70B Attn-48 73.9 -> 66.9, half the layers 71.5 (-2.4%) (Tables 1, 3)
capability.note: Indirect: the drop removes the whole attention sublayer, so attn_core and attn_proj are not separated. Ranked above attn_proj because K/V reduction (GQA) costs almost nothing while removing attention costs several points.

capability.evidence: Output embedding size 768 -> 128 (input E=128): XTREME avg 60.2 -> 56.6 (Table 4); decoupling input/output embeddings +0.4 avg (62.3 -> 62.7, Table 2)
capability.citation: Chung, Fevry, Tsai, Johnson, Ruder (2021), Rethinking Embedding Coupling in Pre-trained Language Models, ICLR 2021 (venue via conference listing only)
capability.note: Multilingual encoder (mBERT-style), not a decoder LM. Press & Wolf (2017) dropped 2026-10-17 (Table 1 recency).

capability.evidence: Factorized input embedding E=128 vs 768, ALBERT-base not-shared: avg 81.7 vs 82.3 (-0.6), 89M vs 108M params (Table 3, Sec 4.4)
capability.citation: Lan, Chen, Goodman, Gimpel, Sharma, Soricut (2020), ALBERT, ICLR 2020
capability.note: Reduction, not removal: no removal ablation of the input embedding exists. Encoder model (ALBERT), not Pythia.

capability.evidence: K/V reduction, T5-XXL uptrained: GQA-8 avg 47.1 and MQA 46.6 vs MHA 47.2 (Table 1); value and output projections fixed to identity: eval loss 1.178 vs 1.194 trained, 13% fewer parameters (146M vs 167M), 18-block 768-wide decoder on CodeParrot (He & Hofmann, Sec 4.2)
capability.citation: Ainslie et al. (2023), GQA, EMNLP 2023, pp. 4895-4901; He & Hofmann (2024), Simplifying Transformer Blocks, ICLR 2024
capability.note: Q is not ablated in any admitted study; K/V reduction (Ainslie) and identity V/output projections (He & Hofmann) are. T5 encoder-decoder with 5% uptraining. He & Hofmann's identity V/P needs their shaped-attention initialisation. Michel et al. (2019) dropped 2026-10-17 (Table 1 recency).

capability.evidence: No positional encoding vs learned: validation perplexity 20.97 vs 20.42 WikiText-103 (247M model), 13.10 vs 13.05 the Pile (1.3B) (Table 1)
capability.citation: Haviv, Ram, Press, Izsak, Levy (2022), Transformer Language Models without Positional Encodings Still Learn Positional Information, Findings of EMNLP 2022, pp. 1382-1390
capability.note: Removes all positional encoding, not Pythia's 25% partial rotary, so an upper bound. Kazemnejad et al. (2023, NeurIPS): similar in-distribution perplexity, differences only at longer lengths.

capability.evidence: Replacing RMSNorm with Dynamic Tanh in LLaMA 7B-70B: avg zero-shot score unchanged (0.513/0.529/0.536/0.549), loss within 0.01 (Table 4); removing normalisation entirely: no usable downstream score (Table 1 'SAS-P, no norm' GLUE '-'; 'unable to remove normalisation with good downstream task performance', Sec 6) (He & Hofmann)
capability.citation: Zhu, Chen, He, LeCun, Liu (2025), Transformers without Normalization, CVPR 2025 (venue via catalog metadata); He & Hofmann (2024), Simplifying Transformer Blocks, ICLR 2024
capability.note: Replacement, not removal: removing normalization outright destabilizes training, so this ranks the norm's function as replaceable, not dispensable. Baseline is RMSNorm, not LayerNorm. Brody et al. (2023, Findings of ACL) give qualitative support only. He & Hofmann confirm removal fails while replacement (DyT) holds: rank 7 means replaceable, not removable.
Training objective, not an architectural component: no capability rank (reported-only in the analysis).
